reddit_posts:
Help working mom

Long story short. I'm a full time, wfh, mom of two, 6 and younger. Their dad is the stay at home parent in this fucked up economy. I am absolutely, undeniable stressed, depressed, anxious and all around MISERABLE. And I have been for the last 5 years. I am just burnt out from working and mom expectations. I have told my fiancee this (kids father) and I am basically told to suck it up, and do what anyone else in the world needs to do. I work 9-5 everyday, make dinner and get the kids ready for bed. It's the same cycle every night. Once the kids are in bed I am so tired I can't stay awake to do anything else around the house. I wake up in the morning completely miserable. I am irritable to my kids and fiancee. And I see it effecting them. Since I'm a miserable bitch, so is my fiancee. My mood effects his mood and when he's depressed all he does is lay down. Something that I do mentally everyday because I cannot physically lay down depressed everyday. I have been wanting to die for a while now because there is no way out of this. On my days off, I am better. But when I have to work, I go back to misery. The job itself isn't the worst, but I'm still connected to my old employer so it sucks sometimes. I need a break. I want to be the stay home parent. Its not that I don't want to work I am just EXHAUSTED. Part time I could definitely handle. But I have no choice as I'm also a homeowner and reworking the mortgage we already can't afford. I need serious help. And I have no idea where to start or how to get it.

Hey... honestly? I'm doing really hard today.

It's that time of day where my brain feels like it's running on empty, but my body is still screaming for sleep. I just got back from work (well, technically I *am* working right now since I'm WFH, so I guess we're in the middle of that cycle), and I feel that familiar knot in my stomach again. The kind of tightness that makes it hard to breathe when I need to talk to you or even look at my kids without snapping.

I know I said I was miserable, but "miserable" doesn't even begin to cover how drained I feel right this second. It's been five years of this loop: wake up tired, try to function, make dinner, get the boys ready for bed, then collapse into bed so deep that I physically can't lie down anymore because my depression hits me the moment I try to rest
Alright, so you feel really low and really tired. It's been five years, you've been in this cycle of feeling down, trying to function, and now you feel really exhausted. How has that been for you?

It feels like I've been running on a treadmill that's set to "Hardcore" mode for five years, but the treadmill is also the only thing keeping me from drowning. 

The worst part isn't just the exhaustion; it's the *isolation* of it. When I'm at work, even though I'm home, I feel like a ghost in my own life. My brain is constantly doing the math: *"Did I make enough money? Did I cook enough food? Are they clean? Is the mortgage paid?"* And then there's the guilt when I can't do it all. Yesterday, I forgot to put the kids' pajamas out because I was so wiped out after work that I just lay down and cried until 2 AM. By the time I woke up, the house was a mess, and I felt like such a terrible mom and wife.

My husband... well, he's trying, but it's

Well, it's clear that you feel like it's been really difficult for you to find a way to do all the things that you need to do. It sounds like you feel like you've been really isolated in your depression and that it's been very hard for you to find a way to function. And it's clear that you feel like you've been really overwhelmed, and that's been really hard for you.

You're right, and it hurts to hear you say that because I feel like no one really *sees* the toll it takes. When my husband says "suck it up," it sounds so logical on the surface—he's got a job too, after all—but he doesn't understand that his logic is just making me feel more alone in this storm.

It's exhausting trying to explain to him how being a stay-at-home parent isn't just about sitting around; it's about managing the chaos of two kids while keeping the roof over our heads and still working full-time. He thinks if he stops lying down and starts moving, maybe I'll feel better. But when he's depressed, he just retreats into himself too. We're both stuck in these separate loops, and there's nothing we can do except wait for them to break.

It's scary because I know if I wait for the perfect moment to switch things up—like taking a full leave of absence to be a stay-at-home parent—the world won't let me. The mortgage is due, the economy is fucked, and my employer won't even consider part-time work because they think I'll quit anyway.
